newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 30.

text.p: The Construction Ministry may start announcing its yearly management evaluation of construction companies that place bids for public works projects, beginning from the business year starting on April 1, 1998. The ministry hopes the move will improve transparency in the tender system by construction companies, both Japanese and foreign, and improve management.

Japan's giant trading house Marubeni Corp plans to set up a joint venture on November 1 to sell personal computer software and music CDs in cooperation with Hiroshima-based computer game sales company Brut KK. The company, capitalised at 200 million yen, will be owned 60 percent by Brut and 40 percent by Marubeni. It hopes for about 12 billion yen in annual sales initially, and to increase the number of retail shops to 300 in five years.

NKK Corp is expected to have increased its parent current profit by 66 percent to 10 billion yen in the first half year to September 30 from the same period a year earlier, helped by a profit increase in its heavy industrial division.

Chrysler Corp plans to postpone the introduction of its Voyager sports-utility vehicle into Japan, which it planned to begin selling by the end of this year, because it is taking longer time than expected to meet Japanese car specifications.

Sapporo Breweries Ltd plans to expand its hop acreage in China to 300 hectares from 250 by 1998, and hopes to to double the harvest in the same year to 600 metric tonnes. The plan includes planting a new variety of hop that produces a more bitter taste. It also hopes to increase total hop sales in China to 2.5 billion yen by 2000.
